answers.how: Measured standing astronaut height at 314 px to set scale (2.2m / 314px = 0.007006 m/px). Tracked root position (belt) to find v_x = 252 px/s and v_y at 0.5s = 87 px/s. Resulting total speed is 266.6 px/s, converted to 1.87 m/s.
Tracked the parabolic trajectory of the astronaut's belt during flight. The constant vertical acceleration is 522 px/s^2. Converted with scale 0.007006 m/px to 3.66 m/s^2.

At 1.0s, the astronaut is in flight at the same relative position in the jump cycle as 0.5s (0.167s before peak instead of after), yielding identical speed: v_x = 252 px/s, |v_y| = 87 px/s, giving 266.6 px/s or 1.87 m/s.
The astronaut is in free-fall flight at 1.0s, so acceleration is the constant 522 px/s^2 or 3.66 m/s^2.
At 2.0s, the astronaut is exactly at the peak of the jump (v_y = 0). The speed is purely horizontal: 252 px/s, converted to 1.77 m/s.
Even at the peak of the trajectory (2.0s), the vertical acceleration remains the constant gravity of 522 px/s^2 or 3.66 m/s^2.
At 3.0s, the astronaut is again at the same relative jump phase (0.167s after the peak). Speed is identical to 0.5s: 1.87 m/s.
The astronaut is in flight at 3.0s, undergoing the constant vertical acceleration of 3.66 m/s^2.
